maya: Quick heads-up — after PTQ 8-bit bring-up for reranker_v2 we see a small regression on the holdout. Ran the standard eval harness this morning.

maya: Summary: NDCG@10 down -0.8% (baseline 0.413 -> 0.409), MRR down -0.5%.
```
model: reranker_v2-ptq-int8
dataset: rerank-holdout-v2 (10k queries)
baseline (fp16): ndcg@10=0.4130 mrr=0.2564
ptq-int8: ndcg@10=0.4097 mrr=0.2542
flags: candidate_prune=0.6, kvpack=false
```

sam: Thanks. Can you paste the eval command and the seed?

maya: eval command: `python -m evals.rerank.run --model reranker_v2 --quantize int8 --dataset holdout-v2 --seed 42 --topk 100`

sam: Two quick asks: (1) can you re-run with candidate_prune off? (2) reproduce with seed=7 and seed=137 to check nondet. PTQ can be sensitive to candidate ordering.

jordan: Also check tokenizer parity between docker image used for fp16 vs ptq run. We had one case recently where a tiny whitespace normalization changed short-query score slices.

maya: Good call. I double-checked the docker tag: fp16 used `redwood/rerank:2026-02-19` and ptq used `redwood/rerank:2026-03-03-ptq`. Tokenizer binary version is the same but config differs (preserve_whitespace=true on ptq image). Re-running with whitespace=false to match baseline now.

eli: Can you dump per-query delta histogram? If changes concentrated in short queries or head queries that points to tokenization vs quant noise.

maya: Will run now. Also toggling `kvpack=true` since KV packing affects memory layout and sometimes quant rounding.

ci-bot: Started job rerank-eval-1717623456 (artifact: s3://redwood-evals/1717623456/run.tar.gz)

sam: If numbers persist, let's run a small ablation: ptq-int8 no-biasfold + calibration on 1k calibration set vs 10k. That often recovers tiny calibration shifts.

maya: Quick interim results (re-run with candidate_prune=off, seed=7, whitespace parity, kvpack=true):
```
ptq-int8 (no prune, seed=7): ndcg@10=0.4124 mrr=0.2558 (delta ndcg -0.15%)
per-query delta: median -0.0003, 95th pctile -0.012, skew -0.08
short-queries (len<=5): ndcg drop -0.6%
long-queries (len>50): no significant change
```

jordan: Interesting — pruning seems to amplify the delta. Could be ranking score quant saturation causing reordering at threshold. Does reranker use softmax temperature scaling before score aggregation?

maya: It does a logit sum over passages and then softmax. I'll dump pre-softmax scores for a few affected queries.

eli: Also run a small MRR-focused run (top1/top3) to see if head hits change more than tail. If top1 is stable but ndcg moves, it's reordering in tail.

maya: Attached a sample of pre-softmax scores for one query (3 candidates) — baseline vs ptq-int8:
```
candidateA: fp16=2.14 ptq=2.12
candidateB: fp16=1.95 ptq=1.87
candidateC: fp16=1.43 ptq=1.44
ordering fp16: A,B,C ordering ptq: A,B,C (same) but score gaps shrink between A/B
```

sam: Shrinking gap is classic quant rounding noise. If pruning uses a fixed absolute threshold, smaller gaps push more candidates below prune cut. Try relative threshold or percentile-based pruning.

maya: Will test percentile prune (keep top 60% of score mass) and also try bias-fold disable.

ci-bot: Job rerank-eval-1717623456 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1717623456/outputs/ (link: https://s3.redwood/evals/1717623456)

maya: Follow-up numbers:
```
ptq-int8 + percentile-prune: ndcg@10=0.4129 mrr=0.2560 (delta ndcg -0.02%)
ptq-int8 + no-biasfold: ndcg@10=0.4126 mrr=0.2559
ptq-int8 + calset=1k: ndcg@10=0.4118 mrr=0.2550
```

jordan: Nice — percentile prune recovered almost everything. That suggests we should change default prune policy for quantized variants or add an adaptive fallback.

sam: Agreed. Action items:
- maya: open a PR to add adaptive percentile pruning fallback when running ptq variants (include opt-in flag)
- maya: add a deterministic-seed smoke test in CI that runs a 1k query eval comparing ndcg/mrr within epsilon
- jordan: add a tokenizer-config check to the eval harness to fail if whitespace/tokenizer params differ between images
- eli: write a short doc on how calibration set size affects ptq quality for rerankers

maya: I'll open the PRs today and drop links here. Thanks for the triage. :thumbsup:

sam: Nice quick loop. If anything regresses after the PR we'll schedule a canary rollback policy for Dedicated nodes serving reranker_v2-ptq.

maya: PRs: https://git.redwood/re/rerank/PR/468 (adaptive prune) and https://git.redwood/re/rerank/PR/469 (ci smoke).

eli: Great — let's also log the final sig test in the rollout checklist so oncall can watch NDCG/MRR trend when ptq is deployed.

maya: Added to rollout checklist (link: https://confluence.redwood/display/RERANK/ptq-rollout-checklist).

sam: Closing loop — will monitor artifact metrics this week.

maya: Thanks all.
